title: Quantum Spectral Model: Data Reuploading with Input-Conditioned Frequency Support
authors: Peiyong Wang, Udaya Parampalli, Casey R. Myers
abstract: A central design principle in modern machine learning and artificial intelligence is to align a model's inductive bias with the structure of its input data. For matrix-valued inputs, relevant matrix-level relationships can be characterised through spectral values and spectral subspaces; however, common coordinate-wise rotation-gate data-encoding unitaries used in most quantum machine learning models do not explicitly construct such a matrix-level representation. We introduce Quantum Spectral Models (QSMs), in which we construct the generator of the data-encoding unitary directly from each input matrix. We study three QSM variants based on symmetric, global block, and non-overlapping patch-local block Hamiltonians. Their outputs admit truncated Fourier representations in which input-dependent spectral gaps supply candidate phase carriers, while spectral subspaces help determine their coefficients. We evaluate the QSMs and comparison quantum models on two matrix representations of Pendigits and two controlled synthetic tasks defined by spectral statistics. At the largest evaluated circuit depth, QSM variants lead the tested quantum models in mean test accuracy across all four benchmarks. The patch-local QSM leads on Pendigits, whereas the global block-Hamiltonian QSM leads on the controlled spectral tasks. Ablations show a task-dependent reversal: subspace-preserving controls perform better on Pendigits, whereas spectral-value-only controls lead among the tested ablations on the synthetic tasks. Together, these results shed new light on quantum machine-learning model design by showing how input-conditioned spectral representations can provide an analysable inductive bias, while offering a broader perspective on structure-aware model design in machine learning and artificial intelligence.
summary: This paper proposes Quantum Spectral Models (QSMs) to improve data encoding in quantum machine learning by deriving the unitary generator directly from the input matrix's spectral properties. By analyzing how different structural components—like eigenvalues versus eigenvectors—contribute to performance on various tasks, the authors demonstrate that structure-aware design yields superior results over standard models.
main_problem: The core challenge is designing quantum machine learning models whose inductive bias explicitly incorporates the structure of matrix-valued input data, moving beyond simple coordinate-wise encodings.
main_result: Quantum Spectral Models (QSMs) consistently outperform tested quantum and classical benchmarks across multiple datasets by leveraging input-conditioned spectral representations. The optimal structural reliance (spectral values vs. subspaces) is task-dependent.
method: The authors introduce QSMs that construct the data-encoding unitary generator directly from the input matrix, leading to an output with a truncated Fourier representation governed by input-derived spectral gaps and subspaces.
model_or_system: The model utilizes Quantum Spectral Models (QSMs) which encode data via Hamiltonians derived from the input matrix (e.g., symmetric or block structures). The architecture alternates between these Hamiltonian unitaries and trainable mixers.
key_observables: Mean test accuracy across four benchmarks, target alignment (KTA), fidelity gap, and ablation performance metrics comparing spectrum-only vs. subspace-preserving controls.
important_parameters: Circuit depth (tested up to 32) and the specific structure of the input Hamiltonian (symmetric, global block, patch-local).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that conditioning the unitary generator on spectral properties provides a superior, analysable inductive bias for quantum data encoding.
figures_summary: Figures compare performance across depths and show diagnostic plots tracking target alignment (KTA) and effective rank evolution during training. Tables summarize quantitative comparisons against classical baselines and ablation studies.
paper_structure: The paper introduces QSMs, details the Hamiltonian construction and Fourier representation, evaluates them on multiple datasets (Pendigits/Synthetic), analyzes performance diagnostics layer-by-layer, and concludes with an ablation study to dissect the necessity of spectral vs. subspace information.
why_interesting: While focused on ML, the explicit use of spectral decomposition and structural constraints derived from physical Hamiltonians ($H(M)$) provides a powerful framework for designing quantum circuits that respect underlying mathematical symmetries or physical conservation laws relevant in AMO physics.
